subject: QBR prep: operations priority snapshot + action tracker
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@acme.ai>, Dan Miller <dan.miller@greencloud.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:15:00 +0000
Subject: QBR prep: operations priority snapshot + action tracker

Team — sharing a compact operations snapshot ahead of next week’s QBR and flagging the asks where I need leadership input. This thread collects the wins, key risks that could affect our latency/cost SLOs, and specific asks with owners and deadlines. I’ve attached the annotated QBR_Priorities_v2.pdf and a short extract of the runbook changes (runbook-sla-exceptions.xlsx).

TL;DR: solid progress on throughput stability; two risks could materially increase host cost next quarter if not mitigated. Please review asks 1–3 below and confirm decisions by EOD Monday 11/16.

Wins:
- Canary for 2nd-gen batching landed on Dedicated; sustained 18% cost-per-token reduction in internal load tests (avg latency unchanged).
- Prefix KV cache pilot rolled to 60% of traffic for the Chat flow (no regressions observed).
- Observability: Route-level token-cost charts now show per-token anomalies for 95th pct — helpful for root-cause of the recent spike.

Risks / Near-term impacts:
1) Spot instance churn in eu-west region (reported by partner infra) spiking Dedicated fallback to hosted variants — potential 12–18% cost delta if we run fallback for extended periods. Impact: Cost (QBR greenfield forecast).
2) A vendor contract (GreenCloud) is delaying delivery of a memory-optimized GPU; if delayed >3 weeks, we cannot scale Dedicated pool for a named account (Acme AI) without increasing unit price. Impact: Revenue/SLAs.
3) Two small regression signals in safety-guard latency when sequence length > 2,048 tokens (rare but high cost).

Asks (owner — decision deadline):
1) Approve a one-time Q4 contingency budget (up to $85k) to cover fallback cost for eu-west if churn continues — owner: Jonas — decision by Mon 11/16 EOD.
2) GreenCloud contract escalation: authorize Soojin to open procurement exception and sign interim T&M to reserve capacity for Acme AI while vendor delivers — owner: Laura — decision by Mon 11/16 EOD.
3) Triage safety regression: allocate two SRE on-call rotations to run extended sequence-length tests and enable targeted quantization guardrails — owner: Karthik — decision by Mon 11/16 EOD.

Action tracker (high level):
- Jonas: estimate contingency draw and signal cap (ETA Mon 11/16).
- Laura: coordinate procurement escalation with legal + GreenCloud (ETA Mon 11/16).
- Karthik: SRE rota + test plan (ETA Tue 11/17).
- Soojin: consolidate final slide for QBR (ETA Wed 11/18).

Notes to externals: Sarah, Dan — including you so you’re aware of the potential scheduling and capacity impacts for Acme’s Dedicated rollout. We’ll follow up if we need to shift timelines.

Thanks — Soojin
--
Soojin Lee
Director, Production & Inference Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments (stubs): QBR_Priorities_v2.pdf (summary + annotated risk pages), runbook-sla-exceptions.xlsx (proposed exception rows)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@acme.ai>, Dan Miller <dan.miller@greencloud.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 10:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: QBR prep: operations priority snapshot + action tracker

Thanks Soojin — solid summary. Quick clarifications: 
- For ask #1 (contingency budget), can you separate the math into (a) worst-case fallback for 4 weeks and (b) targeted mitigation steps cost? I want to see the delta between paying fallback vs accelerating vendor procurement.
- For the eu-west churn, do we have visibility into which Dedicated pools are most affected? If it’s a narrow set of customer accounts we may be able to reroute rather than burn contingency.

I’ll start drafting the contingency note; will aim to have a preliminary figure by EOD Mon.

Jonas
VP, Cloud Operations

Cc: Dan Miller <dan.miller@greencloud.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 09:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: QBR prep: operations priority snapshot + action tracker

Appreciate the clear asks. For #3 (safety latency regressions), I propose the following immediate plan:
- Two SREs (Priya and Marcus) take a 5-day focused rota to run extended sequence-length load tests and collect KV cache profiles.
- If regressions persist, enable the quantization guardrail that caps longest context at 2,048 for affected models and route longer requests to a high-memory pool.

I’ll allocate the SREs and post a short test plan in the Drive link (will add by EOD Sun). If enabling the guardrail is required, that will be a short-lived customer-facing behavior change we should pre-announce.

Karthik
Head of Reliability
